identity.title: Deep ALMA photometry of distant X-ray AGN: improvements in star formation rate constraints, and AGN identification
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We combine our deep ALMA continuum observations with deblended 8–500$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$ photometry from *Spitzer* and *Herschel*, and use infrared (IR) SED fitting and AGN – star formation decomposition methods.

targets.name: 109 X-ray AGN in CDF-S and C-COSMOS (1<z<4.7)

evidence.quote: This results in 109 X-ray AGN with ALMA 870$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$ observations, 101 originally targeted, and 8 serendipitous X-ray AGN.

distance_source.value: Hsu et al. 2014 (CDF-S) and Marchesi et al. 2016 (C-COSMOS) redshift catalogues

evidence.quote: This results in 109 X-ray AGN with ALMA 870$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$ observations, 101 originally targeted, and 8 serendipitous X-ray AGN.

question.value: How much do deep ALMA 870um photometry improve SFR constraints and MIR AGN identification for Herschel-faint X-ray AGN at 1<z<4.7, and can the F870/F24-redshift plane identify AGN?

evidence.quote: We demonstrate that the F$_{870\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$/F$_{24\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$–redshift plane can successfully split between AGN and star formation dominated sources, and can be used as an AGN identification method.
Cycle 1 (2012.1.00869.S; PI: J. R. Mullaney)
Cycle 2 (2013.1.00884.S; PI:D. M. Alexander)
observed with ALMA in Band-7 (i.e. 870$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$)
with a bandwidth of 7.5GHz centred at 351GHz

arrays.value: 12m and 7m arrays; Cycle 1: 32 12m + 9 7m antennas; Cycle 2: 34 12m + 9 7m antennas

evidence.quote: Cycle 1 observations were carried out using 32 antennas in the 12m array and 9 antennas in the 7m array
to obtain a synthesised beam of $\sim$0.8$"$ for all images

sensitivity.value: 0.1–0.8 mJy/beam in CDF-S; 0.08–0.23 mJy/beam in C-COSMOS

evidence.quote: with noise levels of 0.1–0.8 mJy/beam in CDF-S, and 0.08–0.23 mJy/beam in C-COSMOS

time_on_source.value: Cycle 1: 2.5–13 min; Cycle 2: 1–6 min per source

evidence.quote: with integration times ranging between 2.5–13min

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Cycle 1 PI Mullaney; Cycle 2 PI Alexander (authors' own programmes)

evidence.quote: Cycle 1 (2012.1.00869.S; PI: J. R. Mullaney) and Cycle 2 (2013.1.00884.S; PI:D. M. Alexander)
*Spitzer*-IRAC at 3.6–8$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$; *Spitzer*-IRS at 16$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$; *Spitzer*-MIPS at 24$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$

what.value: Spitzer and Herschel photometry assigned to the X-ray AGN

evidence.quote: We make use of the *Spitzer* and *Herschel* photometry assigned to the X-ray AGN in (cite: Stanley15) for our analysis

what.value: ALMA 870um photometry and redshifts of 41 WISE AGN-dominated comparison sources

evidence.quote: (cite: Lonsdale15) present ALMA observations and measurements of 870$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$ of 49 such sources

what.value: ALESS SMG sample ALMA photometry (113 sources used)

evidence.quote: The chosen sample of SMGs is taken from the ALMA-LESS survey (A-LESS; (cite: Hodge13); (cite: Karim13))

external_data_from_literature.citation: (cite: Hodge13); (cite: Karim13); redshifts Danielson17; Simpson14; MIR/FIR Swinbank14

what.value: ALMA 870um photometric catalogues of the sample

evidence.quote: In Scholtz et al. (2018) we present the ALMA 870$\mathrel{\rm \mu m}$ photometric catalogues for the full sample of targeted and serendipitous X-ray AGN

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Empirical IR templates: five SF templates (Mullaney11, extended by DelMoro13) + Arp220 (Silva98) and mean AGN template (Mullaney11); Dale02, Mor12, Symeonidis16 templates for comparison

evidence.quote: This includes the five star-forming galaxy templates originally defined in (cite: Mullaney11), (later extended in wavelength by (cite: DelMoro13)), with the addition of Arp220 from (cite: Silva98)

pipeline_or_manual.value: ALMA data reduction pipeline, with repeat and extra flagging when needed after visual inspection

evidence.quote: The raw data was calibrated using the ALMA data reduction pipeline.
version 4.4.0
and the clean routine in casa
we applied natural weighting and appropriate Gaussian tapering in the *uv*–plane

uv_taper.value: Gaussian taper to ~0.8" beam (values not given)

evidence.quote: appropriate Gaussian tapering in the *uv*–plane to obtain a synthesised beam of $\sim$0.8$"$ for all images

masking.value: cleaned down to 3 sigma from dirty images; sources identified at SNR>=5

evidence.quote: We created “dirty" images, which were subsequently cleaned down to 3$\sigma$. We then identified the sources with SNR$\geq$5.
The resulting synthesised beams are of the size of $(0.8"-0.9")\times0.7"$
with noise levels of 0.1–0.8 mJy/beam in CDF-S, and 0.08–0.23 mJy/beam in C-COSMOS

what.value: ALMA data processing and imaging methods

evidence.quote: The data were processed and imaged following the methods of (cite: Hodge13) and (cite: Simpson15); see full details in (cite: Scholtz18).
We performed fitting and decomposition of the IR SED by following and extending the methods of (cite: Stanley15).
The details of the sample selection for the two programs are given in (cite: Scholtz18)

unstated_but_needed: Exact tclean/clean parameters (taper values, cell size, image size, masks, niter, threshold per field)
Template normalisation/fit routine details and how photometric errors and upper limits are implemented
SED fit code not named or released
Exact photometry values (ALMA catalogue in Scholtz18) needed to reproduce fits
Treatment of ALMA flux deboosting or flux-density extraction method

method.value: Pipeline calibration, dirty images cleaned to 3 sigma, natural weighting plus taper to ~0.8", sources at SNR>=5; upper limits 3xRMS

evidence.quote: If a source remains undetected we take 3$\times$RMS as the flux density upper limit.
We then identified the sources with SNR$\geq$5.
The results were visually inspected, and when deemed necessary, the pipeline calibration process was repeated with additional data flagging.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit IR SEDs and decompose SF and AGN

method.value: Fit 8–870um photometry with six SF templates with and without AGN template, forcing fits below upper limits; choose best fit by BIC (AGN required if dBIC>2); five detection-dependent cases

evidence.quote: The SED fit with the minimum BIC value is defined as the best fit.
the SED with the AGN component has to have a smaller BIC to that of the SED with no AGN component with a difference of $\Delta$BIC$>$2

key_parameters.value: L_IR integrated over 8–1000 um; AGN component counted as significant if >=20% of IR luminosity

evidence.quote: the fit requires an AGN component with a significant contribution (at least 20%)

assumptions.value: Cosmology H0=70, OmegaM=0.3, OmegaL=0.7; Chabrier IMF

evidence.quote: we assume $\rm H_0 = 70 km \, s^{-1} \, Mpc^{-1}$, $\rm \Omega_M = 0.3$, $\rm \Omega_\Lambda = 0.7$, and a (cite: Chabrier03) initial mass function (IMF)

fitting.value: Template fitting with BIC model selection; uncertainties combine formal fit error and range of fits with dBIC<2

evidence.quote: The uncertainties on the chosen $\mathrel{\rm L_{IR,SF}}$, and $\mathrel{\rm L_{IR,AGN}}$ values are the combination of the formal error on the fit and the range of

validation.value: Comparison of AGN 6um luminosity with L2-8keV; test of alternative AGN templates; consistency with Herschel for 2 sources

evidence.quote: The agreement of the ALMA photometry to the *Herschel* constraints provides extra confidence in our SED fitting approach and choice of templates

method.value: Repeat SED fitting with 8–500um vs 8–870um photometry and compare LIR,SF

evidence.quote: we have performed the same SED fitting analysis on the sample with and without the ALMA photometry

analysis_steps.goal: Define and test F870/F24-redshift AGN selection

method.value: Build composite SEDs with 50% AGN contribution, redshift 1–5 in steps of 0.2, take median F870/F24 track; apply to X-ray AGN, WISE AGN and ALESS SMG samples, compare to Donley12 IRAC selection

evidence.quote: This SED is then shifted with redshift steps of 0.2 from redshifts 1 to 5, and at each step we calculate the observed frame F$_{870\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$/F$_{24\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$ ratio.
\log_{10}(\frac{F_{870\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}}{F_{24\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}}) \, = \, -1.19 + 3.623\times \log_{10}(1+z)

validation.value: Comparison against AGN-dominated and SMG samples and IRAC colour selection

evidence.quote: The IRAC colour criteria select 19 out of the 22 sources selected by the F$_{870\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$/F$_{24\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$ limit.

used_for.value: ALMA calibration pipeline and clean imaging

evidence.quote: We used the common astronomy software application (casa; version 4.4.0; McMullin et al 2007), and the clean routine in casa.
In total we find that 40/109 (36.7%) of our sources are detected by ALMA.

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction with measured SFR before ALMA

evidence.quote: (from 2% to 37% of the sample)

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction with measured SFR with ALMA

evidence.quote: we now have $\mathrel{\rm L_{IR,SF}}$ measurements for 40/109 ($\simeq$37%) of the sources

results_numeric.quantity: Sources with MIR AGN component identified

evidence.quote: we can now confidently identify a MIR AGN component in 54/109 ($\sim$50%) of the ALMA observed sample

results_numeric.quantity: Fraction with LIR,SF changed by more than factor 2

evidence.quote: more than half of our sample (67%) have $\mathrel{\rm L_{IR,SF}}$ constraints that have changed by more than a factor of 2

results_numeric.quantity: X-ray AGN selected by F870/F24 limit (of 50 with 4 IRAC bands)

evidence.quote: the F$_{870\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$/F$_{24\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$ limit selects 22/50 sources as AGN candidates

results_numeric.quantity: SMGs selected as strong AGN by F870/F24 limit

evidence.quote: selection limit selects 8/81 sources as having a strong AGN component

findings_qualitative.value: The F870/F24 selection and IRAC colour selection are comparable for strong AGN but both miss AGN contributing <50% of IR luminosity

evidence.quote: both methods are comparable in selecting source with a strong AGN component, but both will miss the majority of sources that have AGN components contributing $<$50% to the total IR luminosity.

claims.hypothesis: Deep ALMA 870um photometry greatly improves SFR constraints for Herschel-faint X-ray AGN
claims.experiment: SED fitting with and without ALMA photometry
claims.result: SFR measurements for 37% vs 2%; upper limits lowered up to a factor of 10
claims.finding: ALMA enables constraining SFR distributions of distant X-ray AGN

evidence.quote: For the sources that still have an upper limit constraint (69/109; $\simeq$63%), the values have lowered by up to a factor of 10 with the addition of ALMA data.

claims.hypothesis: ALMA photometry allows identification of MIR AGN components in SEDs
claims.finding: Large increase in MIR AGN identification

evidence.quote: we can now identify an AGN component in 54/109 ($\sim$50%) of our ALMA observed sample

claims.hypothesis: F870/F24-redshift plane can identify AGN-dominated/strong AGN sources
claims.experiment: Test track on X-ray AGN, WISE AGN and SMG samples
claims.result: All 41 AGN-dominated selected; 8/81 SMGs selected, 7 with AGN signatures
claims.finding: Method identifies sources with >=50% AGN IR contribution

evidence.quote: Overall, 7 out of the 8 sources show a significant AGN signature from additional data

why_this_method.value: Deep ALMA needed to probe typical galaxies beyond Herschel's sensitivity

evidence.quote: in order to directly constrain the SFRs of the typical population of galaxies and AGN at redshifts of $z \gtrsim 1$, we need even deeper observations in the FIR/sub-mm.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Other AGN templates (Symeonidis16, Mor12) tested; Symeonidis16 inconsistent with AGN-dominated colours

evidence.quote: the (cite: Symeonidis16) AGN template is the most incompatible to the F$_{870\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$/F$_{24\mathrel{\rm \mu m}}$ ratios of the AGN dominated sample.

limitations_admitted.value: 14 CDF-S targets observed at too-high resolution, requiring heavy tapering and giving higher noise

evidence.quote: for these observations the images had to be heavily tapered to a resolution of 0.8$"$, resulting in increased noise levels

referee_caveats_inferred: Single mean AGN template dominates results; template-dependence only partly tested
F870/F24 selection calibrated on small comparison samples with heterogeneous photometry
Sample is Herschel-faint selected, so results may not generalise to all X-ray AGN

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA data acknowledged by project code; public status not explicitly stated

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00869.S and ADS/JAO.ALMA#2013.1.00884.S.
